first_impression.reaction: Googled 'mauritius wedding' because it's one of three places on our list and I want to know if the legal side is a mess. The intro answers the question I came with, names the authority and gives the order of steps. No lagoon poetry. Went straight to the FAQ like always: witnesses gets a straight yes this time, recognition is hedged properly, and the links go to the actual Mauritian government pages I can check myself. What bugs me: the ceremony fee is mentioned with no number, and the page keeps telling me to 'ask the Civil Status Office' for things I'd hoped it would answer, like how many days to land before the wedding. Wedded Wonderland stays quiet until the end, which I respect, but it doesn't tell me what they'd actually cost or whether they take a cut.

journey.quote: Mauritius is on the shortlist, and before you fall for a lagoon you want to know one thing: will the marriage count? It will.
journey.reaction: Straight answer up front. That's the question I came with.

journey.quote: In most cases, yes. An overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: Fine on its own, and the hedge is honest. But the intro says flatly 'It will.' and down here it's 'in most cases'. Which is it? Small, but that's the sort of gap I notice when someone's selling to me.

journey.quote: Yes. Two witnesses must be present at the ceremony.
journey.reaction: A yes/no question with a yes/no answer. Good.

journey.quote: Ask the Civil Status Office how many working days to allow, and add a spare day for flights.
journey.reaction: This is the one I actually need for booking flights and leave, and the answer is 'ask someone else'. I get that the government page may not say, but tell me that plainly instead of making it sound like an answer.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Mauritius?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the Civil Status Division sets out a dedicated process for the marriage of two non-citizens who are also non-residents, which is where most Australian couples flying in for their wedding sit.
journey.reaction: A date and a named authority, plus a link to the source page. That's how a legal page should read.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Mauritius?
journey.quote: Read it once, together, before you sign anything with a resort.
journey.reaction: Advice that protects me before money changes hands. Not something a pure sales page would say.

journey.section: What the Civil Status Division asks for
journey.quote: The 3-month window is the detail that catches couples out.
journey.reaction: That's the catch, stated. Exactly what I want: where it goes wrong, not how pretty it is.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: A fee applies for a wedding in a hotel or other premises, and it is paid at the Central Civil Status Office.
journey.reaction: How much? It's a government fee, it should be public. Every resort wedding is going to hit this, so it's going in my spreadsheet. Give me the figure with a date, or link me straight to where it's published.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: If the Officer requests it, you provide transport to and from your venue.
journey.reaction: Small hidden cost most sites wouldn't mention. Points for it.

journey.quote: Ask the Office, too, whether the Officer will ask you to choose a matrimonial regime (the legal arrangement for property within the marriage) and which options apply to two non-citizens.
journey.reaction: Property regime is a finance question and it matters to me. Flagging it is useful, but now I've got a third or fourth 'ask the Office'. The page is starting to read like a list of homework.

journey.quote: Copies are not accepted unless certified by a notary and the Supreme Court, and acceptance rests with the Apostille Office.
journey.reaction: Specific, sourced, and honest that someone else has the final say. Good.

journey.quote: Many couples do exactly that: a long lunch at home for the grandparents and friends who could not make the flight.
journey.reaction: 'Many couples' based on what? Harmless line, but it's an unsupported claim on a page that otherwise sources everything.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach or at your resort
journey.quote: If you offer a wedding package, what exactly does it include for the civil formalities, and what sits outside it?
journey.reaction: That's my question to every vendor. A planner telling me to grill the resort on inclusions is a good sign.

journey.quote: During a cyclone the airport may close and flights may be cancelled or delayed, so check that your travel insurance covers it.
journey.reaction: Honest about the downside, with a source. Skimmed the temperature numbers but they're there if I need them.

journey.quote: If you are weighing two coasts against your guest list, Wedded Concierge can help you compare them on your dates.
journey.reaction: First sales nudge. It comes after the evidence and it's one line, so I can live with it.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Inclusions in writing is the right promise. 'Plans your payments' is where I start asking whether they take a cut from the resort. Nothing here says, and no real Mauritius wedding is shown to back it up.

journey.section: Plan your Mauritius wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Everything around it, from the coast you choose to the hour you marry, is where the planning starts.

unanswered_questions: What is the Civil Status Office fee for a ceremony at a hotel or other venue, and is there any other government charge (certificate copies, Apostille)? The page says a fee applies but gives no figure or direct link to one.
How many working days do we realistically need on the island before the ceremony, from the document check to the wedding?
Does the civil ceremony at a resort need anything extra if it's on the beach itself, or is that purely a resort question?
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee worked out, and what's a realistic range for a Mauritius wedding? (deferred business detail)
Do you take commissions or add mark-ups on the Mauritius resorts and suppliers you book, and will you disclose them? (deferred business detail)
Do you have anyone on the ground in Mauritius, or is it all run from Australia? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real Mauritius wedding you've planned, with the actual budget. (deferred business detail)
How many Mauritius weddings have you done? (deferred business detail)
Are there perks or Wedded Privileges at Mauritius resorts I couldn't get booking direct, and are they itemised? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange flights, guest transfers and the Officer's transport? (deferred business detail)
Will you prepare and send the Civil Status paperwork and handle certified copies or an Apostille, or is that all on us? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Many couples do exactly that: a long lunch at home for the grandparents and friends who could not make the flight.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported 'many couples' generalisation on a page that otherwise backs every claim with a source.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask the Civil Status Office how many working days to allow, and add a spare day for flights.
turn_offs_found.why: The FAQ heading promises an answer on timing and this sentence passes the buck. It's the most practical number on the page and it's missing.

turn_offs_found.quote: A fee applies for a wedding in a hotel or other premises, and it is paid at the Central Civil Status Office.
turn_offs_found.why: Mentions a cost without a figure or a link to one. For someone building a budget spreadsheet, an unquantified fee looks like the catch.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the document list and the 3-month birth certificate rule, for our planning spreadsheet
Our Reddit thread: the resort question list ending 'Get the answers in writing', and the note that the Officer's transport is on us if requested

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, and the promises are concrete: AUD quotes, fee agreed in writing. But my real questions, how the fee is worked out and whether they take a cut from Mauritius resorts, aren't answered. The guide earns them a look at their site, not a call. I'd email those questions before committing to anything.

top_3_changes: Ceremony fee: where the page says 'A fee applies for a wedding in a hotel or other premises', either give the current amount with a source and date (flagged for checking), or say plainly that the Civil Status Division sets the fee and link the exact page beside the sentence.

Arrival timing FAQ: if the source pack gives a minimum number of days, state it; if not, say openly that the Division does not publish one, then give the honest minimum the page does support (document visit, Certificate of Authority, 24-hour publication) so it doesn't read as a dodge.

Tidy the two loose claims: make the intro's 'It will.' match the FAQ's 'in most cases' hedge (e.g. 'In almost all cases, yes'), and change 'Many couples do exactly that' to something that doesn't claim a number (e.g. 'Some couples follow it with a long lunch at home').

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, looked for the catch and the numbers, flagged unsupported claims
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, on-the-ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers and paperwork help listed as deferred unanswered questions, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Top changes require no new business facts; any government fee figure or day count must come from a source

open_questions.question: Does the source pack contain the Civil Status Office fee for a non-Office ceremony, or any minimum days between arrival and ceremony? If yes, the two medium objections close with sourced lines; if not, a direct fee-page link and an explicit 'not published' line are the fallback.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'mauritius wedding' while Mauritius is on the shortlist and he is comparing planners; relevance is 4 because the legal content is what he wanted, and enquiry likelihood is 2 because his fee and commission questions about Wedded Wonderland stay open.
Business details (fees, commissions, ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers, paperwork help) are deferred by the brief; voiced as unanswered questions only.
Rendered link text was quoted without markdown link syntax, as a reader would see it.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, legal and document sections, ceremony and certificate sections, and the Wedded Wonderland sections, with a skim of the climate and coast sections.
